subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Nils Bohlin's Three-Point Belt
description: One-minute skill: Nils Bohlin's Three-Point Belt.

hook.text: Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin designed ejection seats for jets before switching to car safety.

buildup.text: He saw that lap belts failed because they focused force on one narrow part of the body.

discovery.text: In 1959, Bohlin invented the three-point belt—one strap crossing both the chest and lap.

twist.text: Volvo made the patent free so every carmaker on Earth could use it without paying a cent.

climax.text: The three-point belt has saved over one million lives since its invention.

punchline.text: Volvo gave away its best invention to save strangers.

quiz.question: What did Volvo do with their three-point seatbelt patent?

details.summary: Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin invented the modern three-point seatbelt in 1959 and Volvo made the patent free so every automaker could use it, prioritizing global safety over profit.
details.whyItMatters: Bohlin's three-point belt has saved over a million lives since its invention. Volvo's decision to open the patent stands as one of history's most impactful corporate safety gestures.
takeaways: Bohlin designed the belt to restrain both chest and hips
Volvo made the patent freely available to all manufacturers
The design has saved an estimated one million lives globally

faq.question: Why did Volvo give away such a valuable patent for free?
faq.answer: Volvo believed the three-point belt was too important for public safety to restrict. By opening the patent, every automaker could adopt it immediately, saving far more lives than a monopoly would have allowed.

faq.question: What type of seatbelt existed before Bohlin's design?
faq.answer: Before 1959, cars used simple two-point lap belts that only restrained the hips. In a crash these could cause severe abdominal and spinal injuries because the upper body was unrestrained.
